items.d: Record **~354 million tonnes (2024-25)**, up from 332 MT (2023-24) and 252 MT (2014-15). Rice ~149 MT, **wheat ~117.5 MT**, coarse cereals/Shree Anna ~60 MT, **pulses ~25.2 MT**, oilseeds ~41 MT, sugarcane ~450 MT, cotton ~30 million bales. **Horticulture (~355 MT) now exceeds foodgrain output** — the quiet structural shift.

**Net sown area ~140 million ha**, gross cropped ~220 million ha, **cropping intensity ~155%**; forest ~72 million ha; net irrigated area is **~55% of net sown area**, so nearly half of Indian farming is still rainfed. Average operational holding **1.08 ha** and falling; **86% of holdings are small and marginal (<2 ha)** and they operate ~47% of the area.

India is the **world's largest producer (~25% of global output), largest consumer and largest importer**. Production **25.2 MT** on about 28 million ha — the yield is barely 800 kg/ha against a world average above 1,000. Imports ~**6.6 MT**, mainly **yellow peas and lentils from Canada and Russia, tur from Mozambique and Myanmar, urad from Myanmar**. **Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses (2025-26)**: ₹11,440 crore over six years, targeting self-sufficiency in tur, urad and masoor by 2030-31.

India imports **~57% of its edible oil consumption**, ~16 MT worth about **$17 billion** — the **largest single agricultural import** and second only to crude and gold in the import bill. Palm from Indonesia and Malaysia, soy from Argentina and Brazil, sunflower from Russia and Ukraine. **National Mission on Edible Oils - Oil Palm (₹11,040 crore)** and the Oilseeds mission (₹10,103 crore) target 25 MT of domestic oilseed output.

Only about **10% of India's food output is processed** and roughly **2% of fruits and vegetables**, against 65% in the US and 23% in China; post-harvest losses run to about **₹1.53 lakh crore a year**. Food processing is ~7.7% of manufacturing GVA and employs ~20 lakh in the registered sector. **PMKSY (₹6,000 crore)** and **PMFME (₹10,000 crore, 2 lakh micro units)** are the interventions; the **PLI for food processing** is ₹10,900 crore.

India is the **largest milk producer — 239 MT, ~24% of world output** — with **per capita availability ~471 g/day** against the world's 322; the dairy sector contributes ~5% of GVA and supports 8 crore households, mostly landless and small farmers. Fisheries: **~184 lakh tonnes**, second largest producer globally, **largest shrimp exporter**; the sector grew at ~8-9% under **PMMSY (₹20,050 crore)**. Livestock is now ~30% of agricultural GVA and growing faster than crops.
items.s: DAHD Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics / DoF

items.d: Consumption ~**60 million tonnes**; the **NPK ratio is skewed to about 8:3:1 against the ideal 4:2:1**, because urea alone remains under statutory price control while P&K are under NBS. Urea imports ~7 MT and the fertiliser subsidy is **₹1.67 lakh crore (FY26 BE)**. Soil Health Cards issued in crores; **Nano urea and PM-PRANAM** (rewarding states that cut chemical fertiliser use) are the corrective instruments.

MSP is announced for **22 crops plus FRP for sugarcane**, on the CACP's recommendation, and since 2018-19 at **A2+FL plus 50%** — not the **C2+50%** the Swaminathan Commission recommended, which is the core of the farmers' demand. Only about **6% of farmers actually sell at MSP** (Shanta Kumar Committee, 2015), and procurement is concentrated in rice and wheat and in Punjab, Haryana, MP and Chhattisgarh.

Average monthly income of an agricultural household **₹10,218**, of which only ~37% comes from crop production — **wages contribute nearly as much**. Average debt per indebted household ₹74,121, and **50.2% of agricultural households are indebted**. Agricultural credit target ~₹22-25 lakh crore; **KCC** is the main channel, and the **Modified Interest Subvention Scheme** gives crop loans up to ₹3 lakh at an effective 4%.

Agriculture consumes **~78-80% of India's water**; **groundwater supplies ~60% of irrigation and 85% of rural drinking water**, and the national stage of extraction is ~60%, with over-exploited blocks concentrated in Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and western UP. **Micro-irrigation** covers ~1.5 crore ha under PMKSY 'Per Drop More Crop' against a potential of 7 crore ha. Rice and sugarcane take a disproportionate share — the crop-mix problem.
items.s: CGWB Assessment / Ministry of Jal Shakti

items.d: Manufacturing ~**17% of GVA** against the 25% target. **Production Linked Incentive schemes across 14 sectors, outlay ₹1.97 lakh crore** — actual investment realised over ₹1.6 lakh crore, production/sales over ₹14 lakh crore, incremental employment ~12 lakh, and incentives disbursed a fraction of the outlay. **Mobile phones are the standout**: India moved from importing most handsets to **exporting over $20 billion** worth, with Apple's Indian production a large share.

**National Infrastructure Pipeline** — over ₹111 lakh crore of projects; **National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0** for brownfield asset monetisation (roads, transmission, railways, telecom towers). Roads: national highways grew from **91,287 km (2014) to over 1.46 lakh km**, with construction peaking above 30 km/day. Railways: **100% electrification of broad gauge nearly complete**, dedicated freight corridors commissioned, and **Vande Bharat** as the flagship.

India's logistics cost is estimated at **~8-9% of GDP** (NCAER, 2023 study for DPIIT) — lower than the long-quoted '13-14%' figure but still above the global benchmark of ~8%. The **National Logistics Policy (2022)** targets single-digit cost, top-25 LPI rank by 2030, and a unified digital platform (**ULIP**), with **PM Gati Shakti** as the planning backbone.

India handles about **1,600 million tonnes** of cargo across 12 major and 200+ non-major ports; **Vadhavan Port (₹76,000 crore)** is the largest new deep-water project, and **Vizhinjam** is India's first deep-water transhipment port — India previously routed most transhipment through Colombo, Singapore and Salalah. **Sagarmala** and the **Maritime India Vision 2030**/Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 are the frameworks. India's share of global shipbuilding is under 1%.

**Airports: 74 (2014) → 150+**, with **UDAN** connecting unserved airstrips; India is the **3rd largest domestic aviation market**, and Indian carriers hold the largest aircraft order book in the world. **Inland waterways**: 111 National Waterways declared, but cargo movement is concentrated on NW-1 (Ganga), NW-2 (Brahmaputra) and NW-3, and the modal share of waterways remains ~2% against 47% in China.

**GNPA at a multi-decade low of ~2.5%**, down from 11.2% (2018); capital adequacy ~16-17%; the **IBC has resolved cases with a recovery rate of ~31%** of admitted claims but with significant haircuts and delays beyond the 330-day limit. Bank credit growth ~12-15%; **credit-to-GDP ratio ~56%**, well below peer economies — the financial-deepening gap.

Demat accounts crossed **19 crore**; **monthly SIP inflows above ₹26,000 crore** and mutual fund AUM above ₹65 lakh crore — the retailisation of Indian savings. **Financial Inclusion Index (RBI) rose from 43.4 (2017) to ~64.2** — measuring access, usage and quality. Insurance penetration, however, **fell to ~3.7%** against the world's 7% — 'Insurance for All by 2047' is the IRDAI target.

**~484 GW total**, of which **non-fossil crossed 50% in June 2025 — five years ahead of the NDC target**. Solar ~110 GW, wind ~51 GW, large hydro ~47 GW, nuclear ~8.7 GW. But **coal still generates ~70-74% of electricity** because of the capacity-generation gap — always state both numbers together.

**500 GW non-fossil by 2030**; instruments — **PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana** (1 crore rooftop households, ₹75,021 crore), **PM-KUSUM** for solar pumps, **National Green Hydrogen Mission (₹19,744 crore, 5 MMT annual production by 2030)**, PLI for solar modules (~₹24,000 crore), viability gap funding for offshore wind and battery storage, and the **International Solar Alliance**.

Per capita electricity consumption ~**1,395 kWh**, less than half the world average of ~3,500. **Crude import dependence ~88%** and natural gas ~50%; coal imports ~240 MT despite record domestic production above 1 billion tonnes. India is the **third largest energy consumer** and will account for the largest share of global demand growth to 2030.

India is the **3rd largest emitter (~7-8% of global)** with **per capita emissions ~2 tCO₂e against a world average of 4.7**; cumulative historical share under 4%. NDC: **45% cut in emission intensity of GDP by 2030 from 2005** (already achieved ~36% by 2020), **net zero by 2070**. Instruments: the **Carbon Credit Trading Scheme under the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act, 2022**, PAT, and the compliance carbon market from 2026.

**Forest and tree cover 25.17%** (forest 21.76% + tree 3.41%) against the **33% policy target**; mangroves 4,992 km². India has **4 of the world's 36 biodiversity hotspots**, ~8% of global recorded species on 2.4% of the land. Protected areas: **106 national parks and 573 sanctuaries**, ~5.3% of the area; **tigers 3,682 (75% of the world's wild tigers)**, **Asiatic lions 891 (2025)**, elephants ~30,000, and **91 Ramsar sites**.

**Municipal solid waste ~1.7 lakh tonnes/day**, ~91% collected but only about **54% processed**; **e-waste 1.75 MT a year with ~43% recycled**; plastic waste ~41 lakh TPA. **Sewage: generation ~72,000 MLD against treatment capacity ~31,800 MLD**, so over half of urban sewage is untreated — the single most citable number for river pollution. **39 of the world's 50 most polluted cities** are in India.

**~59% of India's landmass is earthquake-prone**, **~12% flood-prone (40 million ha)**, **~5,700 km of the 7,516 km coastline is cyclone- and tsunami-prone**, and **~68% of cultivable land is drought-prone**. India ranks among the countries with the highest absolute disaster losses; economic losses run to tens of billions of dollars a decade. **NDRF ~₹1.6 lakh crore for 2021-26** under the 15th FC's mitigation-plus-response architecture.

India's **gross expenditure on R&D is ~0.64-0.7% of GDP**, against China's ~2.4%, the US's ~3.5% and Israel and Korea above 4.5%. Uniquely, **the government funds ~55-60%** of Indian R&D while business funds most of it elsewhere — the structural weakness the **Anusandhan National Research Foundation (₹50,000 crore, 70% from private sources)** is meant to correct. Researchers per million: ~250 against a world average above 1,500.

Patent filings crossed **90,000 a year**, with **residents filing the majority for the first time**; grants rose about 10x in a decade and the examination backlog fell sharply. India is the **3rd largest producer of scientific publications**, but citations per paper and the share of high-impact work lag.
items.s: Indian Patent Office / NSF Science & Engineering Indicators

items.d: Space economy ~**$8.4 bn (2%)** targeted at **$44 bn by 2033**; **100% FDI liberalised (2024)** with automatic route up to 74% for satellites; 300+ startups (Skyroot, Agnikul, Pixxel, Dhruva). Milestones: **Chandrayaan-3 (first landing at the lunar south pole, 2023)**, Aditya-L1 at L1, **SpaDeX docking (2025)**, **NISAR with NASA (2025)**, Shubhanshu Shukla on Axiom-4. Targets: **Bharatiya Antariksh Station 2035, crewed lunar landing 2040**, Gaganyaan crewed flight.

**India Semiconductor Mission — ₹76,000 crore**; approved units at Dholera (Tata-PSMC fab), Sanand (Micron ATMP, CG Power, Kaynes), Morigaon (Tata OSAT) and Jewar; **the first indigenously packaged chip in 2025**. Electronics production crossed **$115 billion** and mobile exports over $20 billion — but **value addition is only ~20%**, since most of it is assembly. The **Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (₹22,919 crore)** targets exactly this.

**IndiaAI Mission ₹10,372 crore** with 38,000+ GPUs empanelled, AIKosh datasets and safety institutes; India is **1st in AI skill penetration** (Stanford AI Index) and among the top contributors on GitHub AI projects, but private AI investment is a small fraction of the US and China. India hosts the **AI Impact Summit in 2026**. **National Quantum Mission — ₹6,003 crore**, targeting 50-1,000 physical qubit machines within eight years.

Defence budget **₹6.81 lakh crore (FY26)**, ~13% of the union budget; **domestic production a record ~₹1.51 lakh crore** and **exports ₹23,622 crore, up from ₹686 crore in 2013-14 — a 34-fold rise**; exports now go to 100+ countries. Instruments: **75% of the capital procurement budget reserved for domestic industry**, five **positive indigenisation lists**, **iDEX** for startups, DAP 2020, and corporatisation of the Ordnance Factory Board into 7 DPSUs. India remains among the top 2 arms importers globally — hold both facts together.

**Left-Wing Extremism**: districts affected down from **126 (2010) to 38 (2024)**, with 'most affected' down to 6-18; violence down over 70% and the government's target is to end LWE by **31 March 2026**. **J&K**: terror incidents down sharply since 2019; **North-East**: AFSPA withdrawn from large parts of Assam, Manipur, Nagaland and Arunachal, and multiple accords signed (Bodo 2020, Karbi Anglong 2021, Adivasi 2022, ULFA 2023). **Cybercrime**: 65,893 cases (NCRB 2022, +24.4%) and **over 22 lakh complaints a year on the NCRP**, with the **I4C** as the nodal body.
